title: 1987 AHSME Problem 7
statement: If \(a-1=b+2=c-3=d+4,\) which of the four quantities \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d\) is the largest?

solutions.text:
If the common value is \(k,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} a&=k+1,& b&=k-2,\\ c&=k+3,& d&=k-4. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \(c\) is always the largest.

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Set all four expressions equal to one common value
Solve each variable as the common value plus or minus a constant
